advisory.finding: test_every_permissive_omission_states_a_reason asserts on the COMMENT TEXT of the source file under test (check_mcp_models.py), parsing lines and requiring each omission entry be preceded by a '#' line. This is a source-grep/change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving reformat (moving the comment, blank line between comment and entry, reordering entries) with no observable-behavior change, and it tests the implementation's text rather than any runtime contract.
scenarios: A future edit adds a blank line between the comment and the dict entry, or reorders entries — the test breaks though behavior is unchanged.

ABSENCE rationale: no test dumps a TicketStateOut with author/env_id/etc. unset and asserts those keys are absent from the wire, so a regression that adds spurious null keys for a call shape whose reducer does not emit them would pass undetected.
dropped.finding: The core contract that declaring the 39 new properties leaves 'the emitted bytes unchanged' is untested for the newly-declared NULLABLE fields that are NOT listed in _omit_when_unset (e.g. TicketStateOut.author, env_id, bridge_project, repos=[], verify_commands=[], bridge_alerts=[], reverts=[], attestations={}, preconditions_summary={}, source_id, and NextBatchOut.batch=[]). Declaring these with defaults makes model_dump() emit an explicit null/[]/{} for them when unset, whereas pre-change (extra='allow' pass-through) the key appeared only if the reducer produced it. No test constructs a model instance with these fields UNSET and asserts they are absent (or asserts the dumped payload equals the pre-change wire shape). The diff's claim 'The reducer already emits every one of them' is asserted only in a code comment, not exercised.
scenarios: An MCP call whose reducer omits e.g. `env_id`/`source_id`; the declared field now serializes as an explicit `null`, changing the client-facing wire payload the diff promises is unchanged.
